title: Allocator defrag strategy and KV-cache eviction policy analysis
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Summary: Intermittent out-of-memory and long-tail latency observed under sustained continuous-batching workloads. Root hypothesis: interaction between cudaMallocAsync arena growth, the slab / pooling layer and our KV cache eviction behavior causes fragmentation and stranded device memory that is not reclaimed quickly enough between bursts. Goal: produce a deterministic repro, instrument allocator arenas and KV cache life-cycle, evaluate two mitigation strategies (adaptive pooling thresholds + batch-aware eviction vs background defragmentation / arena compaction), and pick a safe production rollout path.
observations: 1) Memory climbs in steps correlated with long sequences and background KV cache pinning during inference. 2) cudaMallocAsync arenas do not return pages to OS until entire arena is freed; frequent small frees after batching lead to internal fragmentation. 3) When KV cache retention time aligns with high concurrency bursts, we observe stranded blocks that prevent arena reuse and trigger new arena allocations. 4) NVTX traces show repeated small allocations (256B-32KB) in hot paths during token generation, causing allocator metadata growth.
reproduction_steps: - Checkout branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feat/alloc-trace-proto (PR link below). - Start a synthetic runner: python ./tools/synth_runner.py --model gpt-medium --concurrency 24 --seq-len-dist long --kv-size 1.2GB --duration 30m - Capture allocator traces: python tools/alloc_trace.py --out /tmp/alloc-trace.json --duration 1800 - Record NVTX and CUPTI counters during run: ./scripts/nvtx_record.sh && ./scripts/cupti_collect.sh - Observe cuda memory via nvidia-smi dmon and our /metrics/allocator_arenas gauge.
experiments: A) Baseline: current pooling + LRU KV eviction -> OOM at 22m on the synthetic runner. B) Increased pool coalescing threshold (pool coalesce_size=64KB) -> fewer new arenas, slightly improved latency but KV tail latencies increase. C) Fast KV eviction for cold prefixes (ttl=60s for non-hot keys) -> reduced peak memory by ~18% but increased rerun rate for regenerated prefixes (quality-impact measured). D) Background arena compaction thread (prototype) -> reclaimed ~35% stranded pages on a 1h run, but increased GPU kernel scheduling jitter in some configs. Metrics: include trace ids and graphs in Confluence (link below).
proposed_solutions: 1) Short term (canary): implement adaptive pooling thresholds tied to observed sequence-length distribution and batch size, plus a conservative KV eviction policy that prioritizes contiguous block eviction to avoid leaving many small holes. 2) Medium term: implement an arena-aware KV evictor that considers allocation/deallocation footprint when selecting victims (prefer evicting keys whose freed memory consolidates into larger free regions). 3) Long term: integrate optional background compaction run (low-priority CUDA stream) with strict safety limits and runtime flags to disable on high-latency SLAs.
tradeoffs: - Adaptive pooling reduces new arena allocation frequency but may increase per-request latency when coalescing happens on hot path. - Aggressive KV eviction reduces memory but can cause quality regressions (more cache misses & re-computation). - Background compaction reclaims memory but consumes GPU cycles and can impact tail latency; needs strict throttling and observability.
decision: Implement short-term adaptive pooling + conservative contiguous-aware eviction as the default for runtime-2.3 canary. Enable background compaction behind a runtime flag and test on dedicated hardware under realistic production traces before broad rollout.
implementation_plan: - ENG: Add arena introspection gauges and NVTX markers (Liam) [done: alloc-probe commit]. - ENG: Implement pool coalescing parameter and tie to sequence-length histograms (Liam). - PM: Coordinate canary experiments with 3 customers and internal testbeds (Priya Shah). - QA: Create dedicated load tests with variable seq-length patterns and KV retention policies (Nadia Rossi). - Ops: Add new metrics to Console: arena_count, stranded_bytes, compaction_runs, kv_eviction_reasons.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for allocator changes. - Integration tests using synthetic runner with multiple seeds. - Canary rollout: 5% traffic on dedicated cluster, monitor arena metrics and tail latency for 48h. - Blocker criteria: any increase >5% in P99 latency or unexplained arena growth after 2x baseline run.
runbook: - Quick triage: run tools/alloc_inspect.sh <pid> to dump arena map. - Temporary mitigation: set ENV ALLOC_POOL_COALESCE=32K and KV_FAST_EVICT=1 via runtime flag to force more eviction. - If OOM: scale dedicated pool up, enable immediate kv-evict-by-size, and collect traces: python tools/alloc_trace.py --duration 600 --out /tmp/oom-trace.json then notify #infra-memory.
notes: Reviewer feedback: - Nadia: add knob to disable compaction per-deployment. - Infra: prefer compaction on low-traffic windows and backoff on high GPU utilization. - Security: confirm no new surface for pointer exposure (checked).
